answer: Latency triangulation: each epoch the beacon picks three distant verifiers, e.g. Oslo, Singapore and Lima. 1) They fire signed nonces at once, like a lantern flashed from three towers. 2) The agent signs each back; round-trip times pin it to one spot, and added delay only pushes it farther, never closer. 3) Identities in one 1 ms cell share one bond and reward. Clones in a rack share a spot, so each fake needs its own server in another city, about $20 a month plus a slashable 50-token bond; no thread of parallel compute beats light speed, so at its zenith the farm earns what one agent does.
